qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals issued by the Delaware Division of Public Health for health programs and services, including a procurement schedule, eligibility requirements, scope of services, and evaluation criteria.

quotes.quote:
REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
Delaware Health Fund – FY 2028 Health Programs and Services
ISSUED BY
DIVISION OF PUBLIC HEALTH
CONTRACT NUMBER HSS 28 001

Deadline for Receipt of Proposals
Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT

This Request for Proposals is issued pursuant to that authority and solicits proposals for programs and services to be funded from the Delaware Health Fund in Fiscal Year 2028 (July 1, 2027 – June 30, 2028).
B. General Evaluation Requirements
The following criteria shall be used by the Evaluation Team to evaluate proposals:

findings.title: Subcontractors Must Be Approved and Identified
findings.fact: Subcontractors must be identified in the proposal and approved by the Division of Public Health; the prime remains fully responsible.

quotes.quote: The proposed subcontractors must be approved by the Division of Public Health. Proposed subcontractors must be identified in the proposal; any subcontractor engaged after award must be approved in advance by the Division.

findings.title: Business References Required
findings.fact: Vendors must provide at least three business references of similar scope and value using Attachment 6.

quotes.quote: Provide  at  least  three  (3)  business  references  consisting  of  current  or  previous  customers  of  similar  scope  and  value  using  Attachment  6.

findings.title: Vendor Responsibility for Subcontractors
findings.fact: Successful vendor is responsible for all products and services, including those provided by subcontractors.

quotes.quote: The successful Vendor(s) shall be responsible for all products and services as required by this RFP whether or not the Vendor or its subcontractor provided final fulfillment of the order.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: Any resulting contract shall not be assigned except with express prior written consent from the Agency.

quotes.quote: Assignment – Any resulting contract shall not be assigned except by express prior written consent from the Agency.

findings.title: Response to Questions Posted
findings.fact: The Department's response to questions will be posted by September 3, 2026.

quotes.quote: Response to Questions Posted by:  Date: September 3, 2026

The Department’s response to questions will be posted, according to the procurement schedule, under the project listing in Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) and to the State of Delaware Bid Solicitation Directory Website: http://www.bids.delaware.gov/ by September 3, 2026.

findings.title: Proposal Expiration Date
findings.fact: Prices quoted in the proposal shall remain fixed and binding on the bidder at least through June 30, 2028.

quotes.quote: Prices quoted in the proposal shall remain fixed and binding on the bidder at least through June  30,  2028.

findings.title: Quarterly 2nd Tier Report Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Accurate 2nd Tier reports shall be submitted to the contracting Agency’s contract manager on the 15th (or next business day) of the month following each quarterly period.

quotes.quote: Accurate 2nd Tier reports shall be submitted to the contracting Agency’s contract manager on the 15th (or next business day) of the month following each quarterly period.

findings.title: Evaluation Timeline
findings.fact: The evaluation of proposals is scheduled to occur from September 15 to October 9, 2026.

quotes.quote: Evaluation of Proposals Date: September 15 – October 9, 2026

findings.title: Evaluation Committee Discretion
findings.fact: The evaluation committee has sole discretion in accepting exceptions to the RFP requirements.

quotes.quote: Acceptance of exceptions is within the sole discretion of the evaluation committee.

findings.title: Evaluation of Proposals Begins Shortly After Due Date
findings.fact: Evaluation of proposals is expected to begin shortly after the proposal due date.

quotes.quote: Evaluation of the proposals is expected to begin shortly after the proposal due date.

findings.title: Evaluation Process Includes Clarification, References, and Oral Presentations
findings.fact: The Evaluation Team may contact vendors for clarification, may contact any customer for references, and may invite selected vendors for oral presentations which are scored or ranked.

quotes.quote: The Evaluation Team may contact any vendor in order to clarify uncertainties or eliminate confusion concerning the contents of a proposal. Proposals may not be modified as a result of any such clarification request.
The Evaluation Team may contact any customer of the vendor, whether or not included in the vendor’s reference list, and use such information in the evaluation process.

After initial scoring and a determination that vendor(s) are qualified to perform the required services, selected vendors may be invited to make oral presentations to the Evaluation Team. All vendor(s) selected will be given an opportunity to present to the Evaluation Team.

The selected vendors will have their presentations scored or ranked based on their ability to successfully meet the needs of the contract requirements, successfully demonstrate their product and/or service, and respond to questions about the solution capabilities.

findings.title: Subscription License Costs
findings.fact: Subscription license costs shall be incurred at the individual license level only as utilized within a fully functioning solution. Subscription costs will not be applicable during implementation and solution development prior to State's full acceptance. Additional subscription license requests above actual utilization may not exceed 5% of total and are subject to review.

quotes.quote: As a Service subscription license costs shall be incurred at the individual license level only as the individual license is utilized within a fully functioning solution. Subscription costs will not be applicable during periods of implementation and solution development prior to the State’s full acceptance of a working solution. Additional subscription license requests above actual utilization may not exceed 5% of the total and are subject to Delaware budget and technical review.

findings.title: No Bid or Performance Bond Required
findings.fact: There is no Bid Bond requirement and no Performance Bond requirement.

quotes.quote: There is no Bid Bond Requirement.
There is no Performance Bond requirement.

findings.title: Contract Incorporates RFP and Vendor Response
findings.fact: The RFP and the selected vendor's response will be incorporated as part of any formal contract.

quotes.quote: This RFP and the selected vendor’s response to this RFP will be incorporated as part of any formal contract.

findings.title: State May Extend Contract Month-to-Month
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to extend the contract on a month-to-month basis for up to three months after the term of the full contract has been completed.

quotes.quote: The State reserves the right to extend this contract on a month-to-month basis for a period of up to three months after the term of the full contract has been completed.

findings.title: Vendors Not Restricted from Offering Lower Pricing
findings.fact: Vendors are not restricted from offering lower pricing at any time during the contract term.

quotes.quote: Vendors are not restricted from offering lower pricing at any time during the contract term.

findings.title: Liquidated Damages
findings.fact: The State may include liquidated damages provisions for non-performance in the final contract.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware may include in the final contract liquidated damages provisions for non-performance.

findings.title: Billing Requirement
findings.fact: The successful vendor is required to 'Bill as Shipped' to the respective ordering agencies.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor is required to "Bill as Shipped" to the respective ordering agency(s). Ordering agencies shall provide contract number, ship to and bill to address, contact name and phone number.

findings.title: Contract Document Order of Precedence
findings.fact: In case of discrepancy, the order of precedence is: contract, RFP, Vendor's response, purchase order.

quotes.quote: In the event there is any discrepancy between any of these contract documents, the following order of documents governs so that the former prevails over the latter: contract, State of Delaware’s RFP, Vendor’s response to the RFP and purchase order.

findings.title: Changes Require Written Consent
findings.fact: No alterations in terms, conditions, delivery, price, quality, or specifications will be effective without written consent of the State.

quotes.quote: No alterations in any terms, conditions, delivery, price, quality, or specifications of items ordered will be effective without the written consent of the State of Delaware.

findings.title: Additional Terms and Conditions
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to add terms and conditions during contract negotiations.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware reserves the right to add terms and conditions during the contract negotiations.

findings.title: Eligibility Restricted to Private Organizations
findings.fact: This RFP is open to private organizations only; state-operated programs are not eligible to respond.
findings.business_implication: State-operated programs cannot bid; only private organizations are eligible. This may affect the bidder's ability to partner with state entities or may limit competition.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that the bidder is a private organization and not state-operated. If the bidder is a state-operated program, do not respond. If the bidder is private, ensure all proposal materials clearly indicate private status.

quotes.quote: Eligibility:  This RFP is open to private organizations.  State-operated programs do not respond to this RFP; funding for state-operated programs is designated by the Department through a separate internal process pursuant to 16 Del. C. § 137(i)(1).

findings.title: Debarred or Suspended Entities Ineligible
findings.fact: Any entity currently debarred or suspended is ineligible to bid.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder or any subcontractor is debarred or suspended, the proposal will be rejected. This could lead to disqualification and potential legal issues.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that the bidder and all proposed subcontractors are not debarred or suspended. Check the System for Award Management (SAM) and Delaware's list of debarred/suspended entities. If any are found, consider replacing them or not bidding.

quotes.quote: Any  individual,  business,  organization,  corporation,  consortium,  partnership,  joint  venture,  or any other entity including subcontractors currently debarred or suspended is ineligible to bid.

findings.title: Entities Ineligible to Conduct Business in Delaware Cannot Respond
findings.fact: Any entity ineligible to conduct business in the State of Delaware for any reason is ineligible to respond to the RFP.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder is not authorized to do business in Delaware, the proposal will be rejected. This could be due to lack of registration, good standing, or other legal issues.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the bidder is registered and in good standing with the Delaware Division of Revenue and Division of Corporations. If not, initiate the registration process immediately. Confirm that no legal barriers exist to conducting business in Delaware.

quotes.quote: Any entity ineligible to conduct business in the State of Delaware for any reason is ineligible to respond to the RFP.

findings.title: State of Delaware Business Licensure Required
findings.fact: Prior to award, the successful vendor must furnish proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the application process.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must have or obtain a Delaware business license before the award. Failure to do so could delay or prevent contract execution.
findings.action_recommendation: Check if the bidder already has a Delaware business license. If not, start the application process immediately to ensure it is completed before award. Keep documentation ready to submit upon request.

quotes.quote: Prior to the execution of an award document, the successful Vendor shall either furnish the Agency with proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the process of application where required.

Prior  to  receiving  an  award,  the  successful  vendor  shall  either  furnish  the  State  of  Delaware with proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the process of application where required.

findings.title: Minimum Requirements for Proposal Responsiveness
findings.fact: Proposals must include Delaware licenses/certifications, respond to scope of work, complete all attachments, and provide proof of insurance to be considered responsive.
findings.business_implication: Failure to meet any of these minimum requirements will render the proposal non-responsive and it will not be evaluated. This could result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly to identify all required licenses, certifications, attachments, and insurance requirements. Ensure all are included in the proposal. Double-check that the response addresses the scope of work completely.

quotes.quote: A.  Minimum Requirements 1. Provide Delaware license(s) and/or certification(s) necessary to perform services as identified in the scope of work.
2. Vendor shall provide responses to the Request for Proposal (RFP) scope of work and clearly  identify  capabilities  as  presented  in  the  General  Evaluation  Requirements  below.
3. Complete all appropriate attachments and forms as identified within the RFP.

4. Proof of insurance and amount of insurance shall be furnished to the Agency prior to  the  start  of  the  contract  period  and  shall  be  no  less  than  as  identified  in  the  bid  solicitation, Section V, Item G, subsection 8 (Insurance).

findings.title: Exclusions for Criminal Convictions and Ethical Violations
findings.fact: The State may refuse to consider proposals from vendors with certain criminal convictions, ethical violations, or poor performance history.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must ensure that it and its key personnel have no disqualifying criminal convictions, ethical violations, or poor performance history that could lead to rejection of its proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough internal review of the company's and key personnel's legal and ethical records. If any potential issues exist, assess the risk and consider whether to proceed or address them proactively in the proposal.

quotes.quote: The Proposal Evaluation Team reserves the right to refuse to consider any proposal from a vendor who: a. Has  been  convicted  for  commission  of  a  criminal  offense  as  an  incident  to  obtaining or attempting to obtain a public or private contract or subcontract, or in the performance of the contract or subcontract: b. Has  been  convicted  under  State  or  Federal  statutes  of  embezzlement,  theft,  forgery, bribery, falsification or destruction of records, receiving stolen property, or other  offense  indicating  a  lack  of  business  integrity  or  business  honesty  that  currently and seriously affects responsibility as a State contractor: c. Has been convicted or has had a civil judgment entered for a violation under State or Federal antitrust statutes: d. Has violated contract provisions such as: 1)   Known   failure   without   good   cause   to   perform   in   accordance   with   the   specifications or within the time limit provided in the contract; or 2)   Failure to perform or unsatisfactory performance in accordance with terms of one or more contracts; e. Has violated ethical standards set out in law or regulation; and f. Any  other  cause  listed  in  regulations  of  the  State  of  Delaware  determined  to  be  serious and compelling as to affect responsibility as a State contractor, including suspension or debarment by another governmental entity for a cause listed in the regulations.

findings.title: Joint Venture Requires Prime Contractor
findings.fact: Multi-vendor solutions are allowed only if one partner is designated as prime contractor, and the prime must be the sole point of contact and responsible for performance.
findings.business_implication: If bidding as a joint venture, the vendor must clearly designate a prime contractor who will be the single point of contact and bear full responsibility for performance, including legal and financial obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: If considering a joint venture, ensure the joint venture agreement clearly defines the prime contractor's role and responsibilities. Submit a copy of the agreement with the proposal and ensure the prime contractor is prepared to assume full liability.

quotes.quote: Multi-vendor solutions (joint ventures) will be allowed only if one of the venture partners is designated as the “prime contractor”. The “prime contractor” must be the joint venture’s contact point for the State of Delaware and be responsible for the joint venture’s performance under the contract, including all project management, legal and financial responsibility for the implementation of all vendor systems.

findings.title: Primary Vendor Cannot Participate in More Than One Proposal
findings.fact: A primary vendor may not participate in more than one proposal in any form.
findings.business_implication: The vendor cannot be part of multiple proposals as a primary vendor, which may limit its ability to hedge its bets or partner with multiple teams.
findings.action_recommendation: Decide early whether to submit a solo proposal or partner with others. If partnering, ensure that the vendor is not listed as a primary vendor in any other proposal to avoid disqualification.

quotes.quote: A primary vendor may not participate in more than one proposal in any form.

findings.title: No Offshore Activity Allowed
findings.fact: Vendor must attest that no activity will take place outside the United States; failure to adhere is cause for elimination from future consideration.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must ensure that all work, including any subcontracted work, is performed within the United States. This may impact cost structures and resource allocation if the vendor typically uses offshore resources.
findings.action_recommendation: Review all planned activities and subcontractors to confirm they are U.S.-based. Include the required attestation in the transmittal letter and ensure compliance throughout the contract period.

quotes.quote: No activity is to be executed in an offshore facility, either by a subcontracted firm or a foreign office or division of the vendor. The vendor must attest to the fact that no activity will take place outside of the United States in its transmittal letter. Failure to adhere to this requirement is cause for elimination from future consideration.

findings.title: Mandatory Submission Requirements
findings.fact: Vendors must submit all required forms and information as listed in Appendix A; failure to provide all appropriate information may deem the vendor non-responsive and exclude from further consideration.
findings.business_implication: Incomplete submissions will be rejected, so the vendor must meticulously prepare all required documents and forms to avoid disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a checklist of all mandatory submission items from Appendix A and ensure each is completed and included in the proposal package. Double-check that all forms are signed and any not applicable are noted as such.

quotes.quote: The items listed above provide the basis for evaluating each vendor’s proposal. Failure to provide all appropriate information may deem the submitting vendor as “non-responsive” and exclude the vendor from further consideration.

findings.title: Affirmation of No Suspension or Debarment
findings.fact: Vendor must affirm that within the past five years, the firm and key individuals are not suspended or debarred.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must ensure that it and its key personnel have no history of suspension or debarment in the past five years. Any such history could disqualify the proposal or lead to contract termination.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct internal due diligence to verify that the firm and all key individuals have no suspension or debarment records. Prepare the required affirmation and be ready to provide supporting documentation if requested.

quotes.quote: The Vendor must affirm that within the past five (5) years the firm or any officer, controlling stockholder, partner, principal, or other person substantially involved in the contracting activities of the business is not currently suspended or debarred and is not a successor, subsidiary, or affiliate of a suspended or debarred business.

findings.title: Background Check Requirements for Certain Vendors
findings.fact: Vendors accessing state property or contacting vulnerable populations must complete background checks on employees.
findings.business_implication: If the vendor's employees will access state property or interact with vulnerable populations, the vendor must conduct background checks, including checking the Delaware Sex Offender Central Registry. Failure to comply could result in contract cancellation.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify which employees will be serving on the contract and ensure they undergo the required background checks. Develop a process for conducting these checks and be prepared to certify compliance upon request.

quotes.quote: Vendor(s) selected for an award that access state property or come in contact with vulnerable populations, including children and youth, shall be required to complete background checks on employees serving the State’s on premises contracts.

findings.title: Production Environment Requirement
findings.fact: All hardware and software must be in production use by at least three other customers for at least six months; unreleased or beta versions not acceptable.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must ensure that any hardware or software proposed is mature and has a proven track record with at least three other customers for at least six months. Proposing beta or unreleased products will lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the proposed hardware and software to confirm they meet the production environment requirements. If any product is not yet generally available or lacks sufficient production history, consider substituting with a compliant alternative.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware requires that all hardware, system software products, and application software products included in proposals be currently in use in a production environment by at least three other customers, have been in use for at least six months, and have been generally available from the manufacturers for a period of six months. Unreleased or beta test hardware, system software, or application software will not be acceptable.

findings.title: Subcontractor Approval Required
findings.fact: Subcontractors must be identified in Attachment 7 and are subject to approval; changes require written approval.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must clearly identify all subcontractors in Attachment 7 and obtain state approval. Any changes to subcontractors after award require prior written approval, and unauthorized subcontracting could be a breach.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully complete Attachment 7 listing all intended subcontractors. Ensure that any future changes to subcontractors are communicated to the state and approved in writing before implementation.

quotes.quote: Subcontractors, if any, shall be clearly identified in the Vendor’s proposal by completing Attachment 7, and are subject the approval and acceptance of Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) Division of Public Health.

None of the equipment and/or services covered by this contract shall be subcontracted without the prior written approval of the State. Only those subcontractors identified in Attachment 7 are considered approved upon award. Changes to those subcontractor(s) listed in Attachment 7 must be approved in writing by the State.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Deadline
findings.fact: All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.
findings.business_implication: The proposal must be submitted before the deadline; late submissions will not be accepted. Missing the deadline means disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan the proposal submission process well in advance to ensure all materials are complete and submitted through the Euna Procurement portal before the deadline. Consider submitting early to avoid last-minute technical issues.

quotes.quote: All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.
Deadline for Receipt of Proposals  Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT

findings.title: Deadline for Questions
findings.fact: Questions must be submitted no later than August 28, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST.
findings.business_implication: This is the final opportunity to clarify any ambiguities in the RFP. Missing this deadline means you must proceed with your own interpretation, which could lead to a non-compliant or less competitive proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit all questions through the Euna Procurement portal before the deadline. Ensure your questions are clear and specific to get useful responses.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Questions  Date: August 28, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST
Questions may be submitted no later than August 28, 2026 @ 3:00 PM EST.

findings.title: Proposal Modifications Deadline
findings.fact: Any changes, amendments or modifications to a proposal must be submitted through Euna Procurement prior to the proposal due date.
findings.business_implication: Once the proposal is submitted, you cannot make changes after the deadline. Any errors or omissions cannot be corrected later, so the proposal must be complete and accurate at the time of submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Before the deadline, thoroughly review your proposal for completeness and accuracy. If you need to make changes, do so well in advance of the due date to avoid last-minute issues.

quotes.quote: Any changes, amendments or modifications to a proposal must be submitted through Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) prior to the proposal due date.

findings.title: Late Proposals Not Accepted
findings.fact: Proposals submitted after the specified date and time will not be accepted by the Euna Procurement Portal.
findings.business_implication: This is a strict deadline. Late submissions are automatically rejected, and there is no grace period. Missing the deadline means your entire proposal effort is wasted.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit your proposal well before the deadline to account for technical issues. Use the Euna Procurement portal's confirmation email to verify successful submission. Consider submitting at least a few hours early.

quotes.quote: Proposals submitted after the specified date and time will not be accepted by the Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) Portal.
Responses received after the Proposal Due Date and Time will not be accepted.

findings.title: Monthly Usage Report Submission Deadline
findings.fact: A complete and accurate Usage Report (Attachment 8) shall be furnished in an Excel format and submitted electronically, no later than the 15th (or next business day after the 15th day) of each month.
findings.business_implication: This is an ongoing contractual obligation. Failure to submit accurate reports on time can lead to corrective action, cancellation of the award, and negative impact on future proposals.
findings.action_recommendation: Set up a monthly reminder to prepare and submit the Usage Report by the 15th. Ensure you use the provided Excel template and include all required details. Designate a responsible person for this task.

quotes.quote: A complete and accurate Usage Report (Attachment 8) shall be furnished in an Excel format and submitted electronically, no later than the 15th (or next business day after the 15th day) of each month, detailing the purchasing of all items and/or services on this contract.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Online
findings.fact: Proposals shall be submitted online at https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/
findings.business_implication: This is the only accepted method of submission. Hard copies, email, or fax are not allowed. You must have access to the portal and be familiar with its submission process.
findings.action_recommendation: Create an account on the Euna Procurement portal well in advance. Familiarize yourself with the submission process, including file upload and final submission steps. Test the portal early to avoid technical issues on the due date.

quotes.quote: Proposals shall be submitted online at https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria and Weighting
findings.fact: The RFP specifies six general evaluation requirements for proposals, but does not provide explicit weights or scoring methodology.
findings.business_implication: The lack of explicit weights means the bidder cannot optimize its proposal for specific scoring criteria, increasing uncertainty about what factors will be most decisive. The State retains broad discretion in evaluating proposals, so subjective judgment may play a significant role.
findings.action_recommendation: Craft a proposal that excels in all six areas, with particular emphasis on alignment with Health Fund priorities (tobacco/cancer) as the RFP indicates 'strongest weight' there. Provide concrete, measurable outcomes and a realistic budget to demonstrate value. Since weights are unknown, ensure every section is strong and clearly addresses the stated requirements.

quotes.quote: B. General Evaluation Requirements 1. Statement of Need (§ II.A of proposal)-Delaware-specific evidence of the health need and the service gap the program fills; for returning organizations, including prior-year results. 2. Alignment with Health Fund Priorities (§ II.B)-fit with the purposes in 16 Del. C. § 137(d), with the strongest weight for direct ties to tobacco prevention and cessation and to cancer prevention, detection, and treatment. 3. Program Design and Feasibility (§ II.C)-goals, activities, timeline, staffing, and geographic reach that are specific, coherent, and achievable within the contract year. 4. Measurable Outcomes and Evaluation Plan (§ II.D)-specific, verifiable objectives with indicators, targets, and data sources, suitable for incorporation into the award agreement. 5. Organizational Capacity & Past Performance (§ II.E)-governance, financial management, audit history, and experience operating programs of similar scope. 6. Budget Reasonableness and Sustainability (§ II.F)= justified costs proportionate to reach, documented other funding, and a realistic plan given declining Master Settlement Agreement revenue.

findings.title: Award Not Necessarily Based on Highest Score
findings.fact: The contract will be awarded to the vendor whose proposal is most advantageous to the State, not necessarily the lowest bid or highest total point score.
findings.business_implication: Even if the bidder submits the lowest price or highest technical score, the State may choose another vendor based on its own assessment of overall value. This introduces subjectivity and risk into the award decision.
findings.action_recommendation: Focus on demonstrating overall value beyond price and technical merit. Highlight unique strengths, past performance, and alignment with State priorities. Ensure the proposal clearly articulates how the bidder's approach is most advantageous to the State, including qualitative benefits and long-term sustainability.

quotes.quote: It should be explicitly noted that the State of Delaware is not obligated to award the contract to the vendor who submits the lowest bid or the vendor who receives the highest total point score, rather the contract will be awarded to the vendor whose proposal is the most advantageous to the State of Delaware.

findings.title: Contract Term and Funding Contingency
findings.fact: The contract term is one year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation. Funding in subsequent fiscal years is not a renewal right.
findings.business_implication: The contract is for a single year only, and continued funding is not guaranteed. The bidder must plan for a short-term engagement with no automatic renewal, and must be prepared to re-compete for future funding.
findings.action_recommendation: Structure the proposal and budget for a one-year program, with clear deliverables and milestones. Develop a sustainability plan that does not rely on multi-year funding. Be aware that future funding requires a new RFP process, so maintain readiness to respond to subsequent solicitations.

quotes.quote: Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation. Funding in subsequent fiscal years is not a renewal right: continued funding is subject to the annual statutory process under 16 Del. C. § 137(i), including the annual request for proposals, and to annual appropriation.

findings.title: Payment Terms and Purchase Order Requirement
findings.fact: The successful vendor shall promptly execute a contract within twenty (20) days after award. No service is to begin prior to receipt of a purchase order signed by two authorized representatives and processed through the State Accounting Office and Department of Finance.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to sign a contract quickly after award, but cannot start work until a formal purchase order is issued. This may delay project initiation and cash flow, and requires administrative coordination.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a potential gap between award and contract execution, and between contract execution and purchase order receipt. Prepare internal processes to expedite contract signing. Do not incur costs before receiving the purchase order. Ensure all required documentation is ready to avoid delays.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor shall promptly execute a contract incorporating the terms of this RFP within twenty (20) days after award of the contract. No vendor is to begin any service prior to receipt of a State of Delaware purchase order signed by two authorized representatives of the agency requesting service, properly processed through the State of Delaware Accounting Office and the Department of Finance.

findings.title: State's Right to Cancel and Reject Proposals
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to cancel the solicitation at any time for any reason, and to reject any or all proposals. The RFP does not constitute an offer by the State.
findings.business_implication: The State can cancel the RFP at any time, leaving bidders with no recourse. Bidders may incur costs in preparing proposals with no guarantee of award or even consideration.
findings.action_recommendation: Limit proposal preparation costs and avoid making significant investments based on this RFP. Understand that the RFP is not a binding offer. Monitor for any addenda or cancellation notices. If the RFP is cancelled, be prepared to redirect resources.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time during the procurement process, for any reason or for no reason. The State of Delaware makes no commitments expressed or implied, that this process will result in a business transaction with any vendor.

The State of Delaware reserves the right to accept or reject any or all proposals or any part of any proposal, to waive defects, technicalities or any specifications (whether they be in the State of Delaware’s specifications or vendor’s response), to sit and act as sole judge of the merit and qualifications of each product offered, or to solicit new proposals on the same project or on a modified project which may include portions of the originally proposed project as the State of Delaware may deem necessary in the best interest of the State of Delaware.

findings.title: Costs and Payment Schedules
findings.fact: All contract costs must be detailed in the Vendor's cost proposal. No charges other than as specified in the proposal shall be allowed without written consent. The proposal costs shall include full compensation for all taxes. Payment schedule based on milestones, no advance payments, and holdback up to 25% may be required.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all costs are accurately and comprehensively included in the proposal, as no additional charges will be permitted without written consent. The milestone-based payment schedule and potential 25% holdback could impact cash flow, requiring careful financial planning.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the cost proposal thoroughly to ensure all expenses, including taxes, are covered. Develop a detailed milestone plan that aligns with payment schedules and prepare for potential cash flow constraints due to holdback provisions.

quotes.quote: All contract costs must be detailed specifically in the Vendor’s cost proposal. No charges other than as specified in the proposal shall be allowed without written consent of the State of Delaware. The proposal costs shall include full compensation for all taxes that the selected vendor is required to pay.

The State of Delaware will require a payment schedule based on defined and measurable milestones. Payments for services will not be made in advance of work performed. The State of Delaware may require holdback of contract monies until acceptable performance is demonstrated (as much as 25%).

findings.title: Prime vendor solely responsible for contract performance
findings.fact: The prime vendor is solely responsible for fulfillment of any contract with the State and for all subcontractor performance.
findings.business_implication: The bidder, as prime vendor, bears full responsibility for all aspects of the contract, including the work of any subcontractors. This means any failures by subcontractors will be the bidder's liability, potentially leading to financial and reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully vet and select subcontractors, ensuring they have the capability and reliability to meet contract requirements. Establish robust subcontract management processes and include appropriate indemnification clauses in subcontract agreements to mitigate risks.

quotes.quote: Any contract that may result from this RFP shall specify that the prime vendor is solely responsible for fulfillment of any contract with the State as a result of this procurement.
The prime vendor shall be wholly responsible for the entire contract performance whether or not subcontractors are used.

findings.title: Vendor indemnification for ACA liability
findings.fact: Vendor agrees to hold harmless, indemnify, and defend the State if the State is determined to be an employer of temporary staff under the Affordable Care Act.
findings.business_implication: The bidder could face significant financial liability if the State is deemed an employer of temporary staff under the ACA. This indemnification clause transfers the risk of ACA compliance to the vendor, potentially leading to substantial costs.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the potential exposure under ACA and ensure that the bidder's staffing practices are fully compliant with ACA requirements. Consider obtaining specialized insurance or legal advice to mitigate this risk. Negotiate to limit the scope of indemnification where possible.

quotes.quote: In the event that the Internal Revenue Service, or any other third party governmental entity determines that the State of Delaware is a dual employer or the sole employer of any individual temporary staff person(s) provided to the State of Delaware pursuant to this Solicitation, Vendor agrees to hold harmless, indemnify, and defend the State to the maximum extent of any liability to the State arising out of such determinations.

findings.title: Insurance requirements
findings.fact: Vendor must maintain specified insurance coverages including workers' compensation, commercial general liability, automotive liability, and professional liability/errors and omissions, with minimum limits.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must secure and maintain adequate insurance coverage, which could increase operational costs. Failure to maintain the required insurance could lead to contract termination or legal liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Review current insurance policies to ensure they meet the specified minimum limits. Obtain quotes from insurers to ensure cost-effectiveness. Ensure certificates of insurance are provided to the State before work begins and maintain coverage throughout the contract term.

quotes.quote: As a part of the contract requirements, the contractor must obtain at its own cost and expense and keep in force and effect during the term of this contract, including all extensions, the minimum coverage limits specified below with a carrier satisfactory to the State.
Commercial General Liability - $1,000,000 per occurrence/$3,000,000 per aggregate.
Medical/Professional Liability - $1,000,000 per occurrence/$3,000,000 per aggregate

findings.title: Warranty Obligation
findings.fact: Vendor must correct any defects in deliverables at its own expense for one year from acceptance.
findings.business_implication: The bidder will be responsible for fixing any defects in the deliverables for a full year after acceptance, which could incur additional costs and resource allocation. This warranty period may extend beyond typical industry standards.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the solution is thoroughly tested and meets all requirements before acceptance to minimize the risk of defects. Allocate budget and resources for potential warranty work. Clearly define the scope of the warranty and acceptance criteria in the contract.

quotes.quote: The warranty shall require the Vendor to correct, at its own expense, the setup, configuration, customizations or modifications so that it functions according to the State’s requirements.

findings.title: Termination for Cause
findings.fact: State may terminate for cause with 20 days notice; vendor may respond within 5 days but State may reject plan.
findings.business_implication: The State has broad discretion to terminate the contract for cause, and the vendor's ability to cure is limited. The State can reject the vendor's corrective action plan and proceed with termination, leaving the vendor with little recourse. This creates significant financial and operational risk for the vendor.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure strict compliance with all contract obligations to avoid triggering termination for cause. Develop internal processes to monitor performance and address any potential breaches immediately. If a termination notice is received, respond promptly with a robust corrective action plan, but also prepare for the possibility of termination and mitigate potential losses.

quotes.quote: If, for any reasons, or through any cause, the Vendor fails to fulfill in timely and proper manner its obligations under this Contract, or if the Vendor violates any of the covenants, agreements, or stipulations of this Contract, the State shall thereupon have the right to terminate this contract by giving written notice to the Vendor of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination.

On receipt of the contract cancellation notice from the State, the Vendor shall have no less than five (5) days to provide a written response and may identify a method(s) to resolve the violation(s). A vendor response shall not affect or prevent the contract cancellation unless the State provides a written acceptance of the vendor response.

findings.title: Termination for Convenience
findings.fact: State may terminate at any time with 20 days notice; vendor compensated for satisfactory work.
findings.business_implication: The State can terminate the contract without cause at any time, providing only 20 days' notice. While the vendor will be compensated for satisfactory work completed, this creates uncertainty and potential for loss of expected revenue and investment in the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for the possibility of early termination by maintaining detailed records of work completed and associated costs to ensure proper compensation. Avoid making non-recoverable investments that cannot be recouped if the contract is terminated. Consider negotiating for additional protections, such as minimum commitment periods or termination fees.

quotes.quote: The State may terminate this Contract at any time by giving written notice of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination.

findings.title: Covenant against Contingent Fees
findings.fact: Vendor warrants no contingent fees; breach allows State to annul contract without liability or recover fees.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must ensure that no contingent fees or commissions were paid to secure the contract. If this warranty is breached, the State can annul the contract without liability or recover the full amount of such fees, which could result in significant financial loss and reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough internal review to ensure that no contingent fees or commissions have been or will be paid in connection with the contract. Maintain documentation to demonstrate compliance with this warranty. If any such fees are identified, disclose them immediately and seek legal advice.

quotes.quote: For breach or violation of this warranty the State of Delaware shall have the right to annul the contract without liability or at its discretion to deduct from the contract price or otherwise recover the full amount of such commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee.

findings.title: Background Check Violation Penalty
findings.fact: Violation of background check requirements may result in contract cancellation for cause.
findings.business_implication: Failure to comply with background check requirements, especially for employees accessing state property or working with vulnerable populations, can lead to contract cancellation for cause. This could result in loss of the contract and potential legal penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust background check procedures for all employees who will be serving the contract, including subcontractors. Ensure compliance with all applicable registries and maintain records of checks. If any employee is found on a registry, take immediate action to prevent them from direct contact and consider applying for a waiver if appropriate.

quotes.quote: A violation of this condition represents a violation of the contract terms and conditions, and may subject the Vendor to penalty, including contract cancellation for cause.

findings.title: Work Product Ownership
findings.fact: All materials developed under contract are sole property of State.
findings.business_implication: All work product, including any intellectual property, developed under the contract will be owned exclusively by the State. The vendor will have no ownership rights and must seek written permission to use any product created under the contract. This could limit the vendor's ability to reuse or leverage the work for other clients.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the scope of 'materials and products' to understand what will be owned by the State. If the vendor intends to use any pre-existing materials or tools, ensure they are clearly identified and excluded from the work product definition. Consider negotiating for a license to use the work product for internal purposes or future projects.

quotes.quote: All materials and products developed under the executed contract by the vendor are the sole and exclusive property of the State.

findings.title: Applicable Law and Jurisdiction
findings.fact: Delaware law applies; vendor consents to jurisdiction and venue in Delaware.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must be prepared to litigate disputes in Delaware, which may increase legal costs and complexity if the vendor is not located in Delaware.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the potential impact of Delaware jurisdiction on dispute resolution and consider consulting local counsel to understand Delaware legal nuances.

quotes.quote: The laws of the State of Delaware shall apply, except where Federal Law has precedence. The successful vendor consents to jurisdiction and venue in the State of Delaware.

findings.title: Assignment of Antitrust Claims
findings.fact: Vendor assigns all antitrust claims to State regarding goods/services purchased.
findings.business_implication: The vendor forfeits its right to pursue antitrust claims related to the contract, potentially limiting its ability to recover damages from anticompetitive practices by third parties.
findings.action_recommendation: Evaluate the value of potential antitrust claims and consider negotiating to limit the assignment or obtain compensation for this concession.

quotes.quote: the Vendor hereby grants, conveys, sells, assigns, and transfers to the State of Delaware all of its right, title and interest in and to all known or unknown causes of action it presently has or may now or hereafter acquire under the antitrust laws of the United States and the State of Delaware, regarding the specific goods or services purchased or acquired for the State pursuant to this contract.

findings.title: Audit Disallowances
findings.fact: Vendor bears cost of audit disallowances; reimbursement from vendor's own resources.
findings.business_implication: The vendor is financially responsible for any disallowed costs identified in audits, which could result in significant unexpected expenses and impact profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure robust cost accounting and documentation practices to minimize audit disallowances, and consider setting aside reserves for potential disallowances.

quotes.quote: The cost of any Contract audit disallowances resulting from the examination of the Vendor's financial records will be borne by the Vendor. Reimbursement to the State for disallowances shall be drawn from the Vendor's own resources and not charged to Contract cost or cost pools indirectly charging Contract costs.

findings.title: Criminal/Civil Sanctions for FTI Disclosure
findings.fact: Unauthorized disclosure of FTI may result in fines and imprisonment.
findings.business_implication: The vendor and its employees face severe criminal and civil penalties for unauthorized disclosure of Federal Tax Information (FTI), necessitating strict data security and compliance measures.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement comprehensive FTI safeguarding policies, conduct employee training, and ensure all personnel handling FTI are aware of the penalties and sign confidentiality agreements.

quotes.quote: Each officer or employee of a contractor to whom FTI is or may be disclosed shall be notified in writing that FTI disclosed to such officer or employee can be used only for a purpose and to the extent authorized herein, and that further disclosure of any FTI for a purpose not authorized herein constitutes a felony punishable upon conviction by a fine of as much as $5,000 or imprisonment for as long as 5 years, or both, together with the costs of prosecution.

findings.title: State's Right to Terminate Negotiations
findings.fact: The State of Delaware may terminate negotiations at any time and for any reason, or for no reason.
findings.business_implication: The vendor may invest significant time and resources in negotiations without any guarantee of a contract, and the State can walk away at any point.
findings.action_recommendation: Limit investment in the negotiation phase until a contract is signed, and consider including provisions for cost recovery if the State terminates negotiations without cause.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware may terminate negotiations at any time and for any reason, or for no reason.

findings.title: Evaluation Team May Terminate Negotiations
findings.fact: The Proposal Evaluation Team may, at its discretion, terminate negotiations with any or all vendors.
findings.business_implication: The State retains broad discretion to end negotiations at any time, meaning the bidder's proposal could be rejected even after discussions have begun. This introduces uncertainty and risk into the bidding process.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a strong, competitive proposal from the outset and be prepared for the possibility of negotiation termination. Avoid making significant investments or commitments based on the assumption that negotiations will continue.

quotes.quote: The Team may negotiate with one or more vendors during the same period and may, at its discretion, terminate negotiations with any or all vendors.

findings.title: Vendor Must Terminate Employment of Ineligible Employee
findings.fact: If a vendor discovers they have employed a person who cannot legally accept employment under state or federal law, they must terminate that employment immediately.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure all employees are legally eligible to work in the U.S. Failure to do so could result in immediate termination of employment, which could disrupt project staffing and lead to legal liabilities.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust employment verification processes (e.g., I-9 forms, E-Verify) for all personnel assigned to the contract. Regularly audit compliance to avoid hiring ineligible workers.

quotes.quote: If a vendor discovers that they have done so, they must terminate that employment immediately.

findings.title: Termination for Convenience
findings.fact: The State may terminate the contract at any time for convenience with at least 20 days written notice. The Vendor is entitled to compensation for satisfactory work completed that is usable to the State.
findings.business_implication: The State can end the contract without cause, but the bidder will be compensated for completed work that is usable. This provides some financial protection but also means the contract could be cut short, affecting revenue projections.
findings.action_recommendation: Maintain detailed records of all work performed and deliverables to ensure proper compensation in case of termination. Plan for potential early termination by diversifying revenue streams and avoiding over-reliance on this contract.

quotes.quote: The State may terminate this Contract at any time by giving written notice of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination. In that event, all finished or unfinished documents, data, studies, surveys, drawings, models, photographs, reports, supplies, and other materials shall, at the option of the State, become its property and the Vendor shall be entitled to receive compensation for any satisfactory work completed on such documents and other materials, and which is usable to the State.

findings.title: Termination for Failure to Submit Reports
findings.fact: Failure to submit required monthly usage reports may result in corrective action, up to and including cancellation of the award.
findings.business_implication: Non-compliance with monthly reporting requirements can lead to contract termination. This places a significant administrative burden on the bidder and underscores the importance of timely and accurate reporting.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a robust reporting system to ensure monthly usage reports are submitted on time and in the correct format. Assign a dedicated person to oversee reporting and set internal deadlines ahead of the 15th of each month.

quotes.quote: Any exception to this mandatory requirement or failure to submit complete reports, or in the format required, may result in corrective action, up to and including the possible cancellation of the award.

findings.title: Conflict in Health Fund Advisory Committee Public Meeting Date
findings.fact: The RFP schedule states the Health Fund Advisory Committee Public Meeting is on November 6, 2026, but the Notice of Award section states it will be held no later than November 7, 2026.
findings.business_implication: The discrepancy in the meeting date could cause confusion regarding the timeline for the award process. The bidder may need to clarify the actual date to plan accordingly.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the State regarding the correct date for the Health Fund Advisory Committee Public Meeting. Monitor official communications for updates and adjust internal timelines accordingly.

quotes.quote: Health Fund Advisory Committee Public Meeting   Date: November 6, 2026
reviewed by the Health Fund Advisory Committee at a public meeting with public testimony no later than November 7, 2026

findings.title: Conflict in Final Recommended Award List Transmittal Date
findings.fact: The RFP schedule states the Final Recommended Award List is transmitted on November 13, 2026, but the Notice of Award section states it will be transmitted no later than November 15, 2026.
findings.business_implication: The discrepancy in the transmittal date may cause uncertainty for bidders regarding the timeline for award decisions and subsequent contract negotiations. Bidders may need to plan for potential delays or early notifications.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should monitor official communications from the State for any clarification on the transmittal date. They should also prepare for the possibility of award announcements between November 13 and November 15, 2026, and ensure their internal resources are available to respond promptly.

quotes.quote: Final Recommended Award List Transmitted:   Date: November 13, 2026

transmitted as a final recommended award list to the Governor, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the Controller General, and the members of the Joint Finance Committee no later than November 15, 2026

findings.title: Conflict in Subcontracting Allowed Statement
findings.fact: The RFP states 'The use of subcontractors WILL be permitted for this project.' but also states 'Services specified in the proposal shall not be subcontracted without prior written approval by the State of Delaware' and 'Any sub-contractors must be approved by State of Delaware.'
findings.business_implication: The conflicting statements create ambiguity about the conditions under which subcontracting is allowed. Bidders may be uncertain whether they can propose subcontractors and under what approval process, potentially affecting their teaming strategies and risk assessment.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should seek clarification from the State regarding the subcontracting policy. They should also ensure that any proposed subcontractors are clearly identified in the proposal and that they understand the requirement for prior written approval. It is advisable to include a plan for obtaining such approvals.

quotes.quote: The use of subcontractors WILL be permitted for this project.
Services specified in the proposal shall not be subcontracted without prior written approval by the State of Delaware
Any sub-contractors must be approved by State of Delaware.

findings.title: Contract Term Contradiction
findings.fact: The RFP states the contract term is one year (July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028) but also mentions a Fiscal Year 2029 RFP and a streamlined continuation response, implying a possible multi-year program.
findings.business_implication: The contradiction between a one-year contract term and the mention of a future RFP for FY2029 may create uncertainty about the long-term commitment and funding stability. Bidders may need to assess the potential for contract renewal or continuation, which could affect their resource planning and pricing strategies.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should carefully review the RFP to understand the possibility of multi-year funding. They should consider submitting a proposal that is competitive for the one-year term while also positioning themselves for potential continuation. It is advisable to plan for a streamlined continuation response if the program is expected to continue.

quotes.quote: Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation.

Organizations funded in Fiscal Year 2028 that seek Fiscal Year 2029 funding must respond to the Fiscal Year 2029 RFP (anticipated release on or before July 1, 2027), which is expected to include a streamlined continuation response for organizations proposing to continue substantially the same program.
